connector: The children are walking now, through wild woods and up to the edge of a deep gorge. Lucy sees something the others don’t, and the group has to vote. Watch each person weigh the choice. A vote tells you what someone values.

a.raw: although lucy saw aslan clearly the others kept walking because they could not see him at all
a.fixed: Although Lucy saw Aslan clearly, the others kept walking because they could not see him at all.
a.why: Capitals on Although, Lucy and Aslan; a comma after the opening although clause; no comma before because at the end; a period ends it.

b.raw: because edmund remembered being wrong before he voted to believe lucy
b.fixed: Because Edmund remembered being wrong before, he voted to believe Lucy.
b.why: Capitals on Because, Edmund and Lucy; a comma after the opening because clause; a period ends it.

scholar.journal-q3: … and say what the plain words leave out.

s4w28cf1.h1: Think of finite. Which vowel do you hear clearly there?
s4w28cf1.why: fin-ITE: the vowel is i, so definite.

s4w28cf2.h1: Think of composite. Which vowel is stressed there?
s4w28cf2.why: com-POS-ite: the vowel is i, so composition.

s4w28cf3.h1: Think of apart: separate means pulled apart. Which vowel?
s4w28cf3.why: a-PART: the vowel is a, so separate.

s4w28cf4.h1: Think of councillor. Which consonant follows coun-?

notes.wgrd: At the gorge, find the exact decision, weigh it from each voter’s side, and count what the choice costs.
vocab: A group gathered to talk and decide what to do.
The chief steward who runs a lord’s household.
Ditches and banks dug for defense.
Companions, especially of a king or queen.
A deep, narrow valley with steep sides.
A rough camp without proper shelter.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: spect = look, ject = throw, script and scribe = write: inspect, reject, manuscript, spectacles.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main clause and a dependent clause that starts with a word like because, although, when, if or since. If the dependent clause comes first, put a comma after it. Although and because let one sentence hold the doubt and the reason.
notes.spelling: Schwa is the lazy uh sound in an unstressed syllable. Your ear can’t spell it, so find a related word where that vowel is stressed: definite from finite, composition from compose.

catcher.title: The vote at the gorge
catcher.intro: As you read Ch. 9, record each vote.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: In Chapter 9 the group votes on which way to go. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Edmund says, “It was Lucy who discovered it first and none of us would believe her. I was the worst of the lot, I know.”
items.why: He admits his old mistake in front of everyone.

items.t: Susan says, “Don’t be angry, Lu, but I do think we should go down. I’m dead tired.”
items.why: She tells the truth about how she feels, and says it gently.

items.t: Peter says he’d much rather not have to vote. Trumpkin answers sternly, “You’re the High King.”
items.why: Trumpkin reminds Peter that deciding is his job.

items.t: Peter says, “I know Lucy may be right after all, but I can’t help it. We must do one or the other.”
items.why: He makes the hard call and admits he might be wrong.
items.hint: What does Peter admit, and what does he still do?

virtue.kicker: Seven Pillars Watch · after you read
virtue.name: pillars

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. The children are on foot now, and they come to the edge of a deep gorge. Today’s question: what does a vote tell you about the person who casts it?
transcripts.read: Read the vote slowly. Listen to each person’s reason: Trumpkin, Susan, Edmund, then Peter. Nobody is silly here. Each one is weighing something real. Then notice the very last sentence of the chapter, and how plain it is.
transcripts.spelling: Schwa is the lazy uh sound in a word. You can’t hear which vowel it is. So find a cousin of the word where the vowel is loud. Opposite sounds like uh in the middle. But oppose says its o clearly. So opposite has an o.
